# Header drawings and preset dashes

Original OPC/XML fixtures generated by `tools/header_drawing_fixture.py`, with
original solid-color PNGs generated using Python's standard library. No corpus
artwork or third-party document engine is included.

References were exported by the reference application on 2026-09-18.
`reference.json` records source/PDF hashes, page counts, PDF dash operands,
line coordinates and image transforms. Header crops use PDFium at 96 DPI.
All five reference documents have three pages. The header is repeated on each.

The main fixture has eleven 2 pt preset line styles, a full-height center line,
a green inline header image, a blue inline footer image and a red body image.
All three image relationships deliberately use `paint` as their ID. Header and
footer parts live in a subdirectory and resolve `../media` independently.
A dashed footer drawing uses paragraph-relative vertical positioning.

The effect controls add 1.5 pt right/bottom effect extents and center the anchor:

| Control | Inner frame, pt | Frame x, pt | Vertical line x, pt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Percentage page size | 610.5 × 790.5 | 0 | 305.25 |
| Fixed 612 × 792 pt size | 612 × 792 | -0.75 | 305.25 |

The percentage size covers the frame plus effect extents. Alignment includes
the extents for both controls. These probes explain the placement of the cut
and fold guides in a corpus document without document-specific
coordinates in the renderer.

The footer controls distinguish the final paragraph mark from actual text:

| Footer ending | Blue image top, pt from page top | Bottom, pt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image only, then its paragraph mark | 738 | 774 |
| Image followed by `g` | 735.669 | 771.669 |
| Image paragraph followed by an empty paragraph | 723.348 | 759.348 |

The reference application omits the invisible mark's bottom clearance for the final image-only
single-spaced footer line. Visible text and a following empty paragraph retain
their clearance. The implementation leaves other line-spacing modes unchanged.
This is observed reference layout detail, not a claim of contradictory normative
OOXML text. Preset dash operands agree with the binary patterns in ECMA-376
Part 1 §20.1.10.49.

Browser tests compare purple header ink with the independent PDF crops on all
three pages, allowing one raster pixel at edges; verify story-local colors and
footer placement; and preserve original downloads byte-for-byte.
Exact text/blank footer clearance comparisons require locally installed Arial;
color, image dimensions and placement sanity checks also run with substitutions.
Unit tests exercise relative dimensions, malformed values, missing/external relationships,
effect alignment and exact edit/undo package preservation. The separate body
fixture permits typing around the same drawing and reopening its export.
That browser export was also reopened in the reference application: one page, edited text present,
and the original dash operands retained. Its transient PDF is kept in the
session workspace rather than committed as a stable fixture reference.

Header/footer editing, story tables/hyperlinks/charts, body clearance around
oversized stories and wrapping story anchors remain outside this iteration.

Validation: 93 focused unit tests and 12 browser tests passed; the six original
fixtures and edited/undo browser exports passed the transitional and supported
extension schema checks. The production build and license audit passed. That corpus
document retained all ZIP parts on download, with zero changed colored artwork
pixels after restoring its neutral cut/fold guides. Header/footer editing remains
read-only.

Subsequent retained-story support enables body editing for these original
fixtures. The independent reference artwork comparisons remain unchanged. Tests now
also verify body edits, repeat drawings after repagination, preserve story XML,
relationships and assets through export/reopen, and restore every package entry
on undo. Direct header/footer editing remains unavailable.
